lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabal was a wealthy man in Maon, and his servants grazed his sheep in Carmel. David and his men had protected those flocks through the winter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the shearing came, David sent men to ask Nabal for a gift. Nabal answered with insults and a curse.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: By the living God, I will not spare one man of this household. Go and get your swords ready.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A servant ran ahead and told Nabal's wife. Abigail was beautiful and wise. She loaded two donkeys with bread, wine, figs, and raisins.

lines.speaker: abigail
lines.text: My lord, let your hand be blessed. Take this gift. I have come to speak for the men of the house, for Nabal is a fool.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: The LORD has kept me from harming you. Go in peace. Your wisdom has saved your household from death.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ten days later the LORD struck Nabal and he died. David took Abigail to be his wife.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: A woman's quiet speech turned a band of men away from slaughter. Mercy spoken at the right moment is worth more than a sword.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David's men named her a blessing. The wilderness had taught him restraint, and Abigail taught him that restraint has a voice.

choices.label: Hold fast to her counsel
choices.note: A wise companion keeps a king from the worst of himself.

choices.label: Keep the sword close for next time ⚔️
choices.note: The wilderness is wide, and not every insult comes with a gift.
